when: before 2:00, all four bot laners are level 1
asks: do we fight level one
should we fight for level two
can we trade at level one
do I walk up level 1
who wins level one bot
say: Walk up and hit the first minions with your marksman to reach level 2 first, or give the push and stay healthy if they hit harder.
more: Level 2 arrives partway through the second wave, so the pair that kills minions faster gets a few seconds with an extra ability each.
Fighting for it costs health and often your own wave position: you end up pushed toward their tower right as the first jungle clears finish.
Giving it is cheap if you stay full health. You lose a few minions, and the wave ends up near your tower where a gank cannot reach you.
check: Which pair has stronger level-one abilities and longer range, and whether their support is already standing in the lane bush.
breaks: If both of you are melee or short ranged into two ranged champions, do not walk up; take the wave near your tower instead.

when: you and your marksman are level 2 and both enemy bot laners are level 1
asks: we hit two first do I go
we got level two do I engage
should I all in now
level 2 go in
can I engage level two
say: Go on whoever stepped up for a minion while you have the extra ability, or just zone them off the wave if they already backed off.
more: The window is short: it closes as soon as they finish the minions that give their own level 2. A late engage is an even fight.
Even without a kill, forcing a summoner spell here makes the next few minutes of lane yours, and it tells your jungler where to come.
Zoning instead costs you nothing and still denies them minions and experience while your wave pushes.
check: How far from their tower they are standing, how much of their wave is alive to hit you, and where their jungler started.
breaks: If they are already under tower or their wave is much bigger than yours, hold the engage and take the free push instead.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

when: an enemy bot laner is level 2 and you are level 1
asks: they got level two first
they hit two before us what do I do
they're level 2 do I back off
we lost the push now what
say: Step back behind your minions until you hit level 2 as well, or hold your ground only if you're both healthy and near your tower.
more: For a few seconds they have one more ability each. Most early bot lane deaths happen exactly here, to an engage you could have walked away from.
Backing off loses a couple of minions. Dying loses the whole wave, the level race and usually a summoner spell too.
Once you are both level 2 the lane is even again and you can step back up.
check: Whether their support has a hook, dash or stun, and how many minions you still need for your own level.
breaks: If their pair has no way to reach you, such as two short-range poke champions, you can keep farming at range rather than giving up the wave.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

when: you are level 2 and both enemy bot laners are level 1
asks: I'm an enchanter do we fight at two
we got two first but I can't engage
level two as a shield support what do I do
do I poke at level 2
say: Stand level with your marksman and trade autos with your shield ready while they're a level down, or simply hold the push if you're low.
more: You cannot start the fight, but an extra ability on your side wins any short trade they accept in this window.
The aim is health, not a kill. A marksman poked low before the first recall has to give up minions for the next two waves.
If you are already low, the level lead is better spent on pushing the wave in and getting a ward down.
check: Whether their support can engage on you while you stand forward, and how much mana a full trade would cost you.
breaks: If their support is an engage champion with full health, standing level with your marksman makes you the target; stay a step behind instead.

asks: when do I poke
when should I throw my poke
do I just spam abilities
how do I poke without running out of mana
when do I harass
say: Poke when their marksman steps in for a last hit, since they can't dodge and farm at once, or save mana if your jungler is coming.
more: A marksman going for a minion is standing still for a moment in a place you can predict. That is the easy hit.
Poke that lands on minions pushes your wave toward their tower, which makes you easier to gank. Aim at champions unless you want the push.
Health you take off now decides who can stay for the next wave and who has to recall on a bad timing.
check: Your mana, whether their support can heal the damage back, and which minions are about to die.
breaks: If their support out-heals your poke, stop spending mana on it and switch to protecting your marksman's farm until an item or level 6.

when: your marksman has more kills or clearly more CS than theirs
asks: do I engage or peel
should I be going in or protecting
am I supposed to start fights
do I engage or stay back with my adc
say: Start the fights while your marksman is ahead, because they win the damage race, or switch to peeling once their jungler shows near bot.
more: A lead on your marksman is only worth something if fights happen. Waiting lets the other lane farm back into the game.
Each kill or forced recall here becomes plates, then the tower, and that frees you both to move to dragon or mid.
The risk grows with the lead: the stronger your lane, the more likely their jungler visits it.
check: Where their jungler was last seen, and whether your engage ability and your marksman's main damage ability are both ready.
breaks: If you are pushed past the middle of the lane with no ward in the river, shorten the fights and back off after one rotation.

when: your marksman has more deaths than kills and less CS than theirs
asks: my adc is behind do I still engage
we're losing lane what do I do
should I stop going in
adc is feeding how do I play
how do I trade when we're behind
say: Stop starting fights and stand between your marksman and their engage so they can farm, or look for a pick only when your jungler arrives.
more: When your marksman is behind, your engage starts a fight their damage wins. The same button used second, on whoever dives, is still strong.
The goal becomes giving nothing more: every wave your marksman collects under tower narrows the gap without any risk.
A behind lane usually gets dived next. Keeping your crowd control for that moment is how the lane comes back.
check: Whether the wave is near your tower, and whether their pair has the tools to dive you.
breaks: If their lane walks up carelessly past the middle with your jungler close, that is the one time to engage from behind.
basis: pro:The lane without help gives nothing

when: the enemy support is dead or has been gone from lane and their marksman is alive
asks: their support is dead what do we do
it's a two v one now
support died do we dive the adc
their support left do we go in
say: Zone their marksman off the wave together so they lose minions and experience, or shove it in fast and recall if you both carry gold.
more: Two against one, their marksman cannot step up to last hit without taking a trade they lose. Every minion denied is permanent.
A dive is possible but costs you if it fails. Starving them is slower and nearly free.
Shoving and recalling instead turns the death into an item lead that lasts after their support comes back.
check: The dead support's respawn timer, how big the wave is, and whether their jungler could cover the lane.
breaks: If their jungler is likely on your side of the map, do not stand past the wave zoning; push it into the tower and leave.

when: the enemy marksman is dead and their support is alive
asks: we killed the adc what now
their adc is dead do I chase the support
adc died do we push
got the kill what should I do next
say: Shove the wave under their tower so their marksman misses it, or drop a deep ward and recall together if the wave is already crashing.
more: The kill is paid in full only if minions die to their tower while the marksman is gone. Otherwise they walk back to a full wave.
Chasing the support through their jungle usually costs more time than the kill is worth and leaves the wave untouched.
A ward on their jungle entrance now shows you the jungler's next visit to this lane.
check: The marksman's respawn timer against how long the wave takes to push, and your own gold.
breaks: If the wave is stuck near your own tower, you cannot crash it in time; hold it there and take the plates window later instead.
basis: pro:Kills are not a lead if the farm went the other way

when: your marksman is dead and you are alive
asks: my adc died do I stay
adc is dead what do I do in lane
should I stay for xp alone
I'm alone bot what now
say: Stay near your tower and soak the experience, last hitting what would die to the tower anyway, or recall now if you have gold to spend.
more: Minions killed by your tower with nobody near them give nothing. Standing in range keeps your level up and saves some of the wave.
Alone you are the dive target, so stay where the tower covers you and give up anything further forward.
A recall now lines your return up with your marksman's, so you walk back to lane together.
check: Your marksman's respawn timer, whether both enemies are still in lane, and where the wave is.
breaks: If both enemies and their jungler are bot and the wave is under your tower, leave the tower rather than die defending it alone.

when: you are level 6 and the enemy bot laners are level 5
asks: I hit six first do I go
I got my ult do we fight
level 6 all in
should I use my ult now
we're six they're five
say: Look for the fight now while you have an ultimate and they don't, or hold it for the dragon fight if they're hugging their tower.
more: An ultimate against none is the biggest single edge the lane phase gives a support. It ends when they finish their own level.
If the fight is not there, the ultimate is just as strong at the river, where the same level gap applies to whoever shows up.
Used and wasted, it leaves you without it when they hit 6 and look for you.
check: Whether your marksman is close to 6 as well, their summoner spells, and how far up the lane they stand.
breaks: If your marksman is low or far behind in items, the ultimate will not make the fight winnable; keep it to defend instead.
basis: pro:Do not fight an objective one spike behind

when: an enemy bot laner is level 6 and you and your marksman are level 5
asks: they're six and we're not
they hit six first
do I respect their ult
they have ult we don't what do I do
say: Play back toward your tower until you both hit 6, giving a few minions, or keep trading at range if their ultimates can't reach you.
more: For the next wave or so they can start a fight you cannot answer. This is the window they have been waiting for.
The cost of respecting it is small and temporary. The cost of ignoring it is usually a double kill and the tower plates.
Tell your marksman out loud. Most lost fights here come from one of the two not noticing the level.
check: Which of their champions hit 6, what that ultimate does, and how many minions you need for yours.
breaks: If only their enchanter hit 6 and their marksman has not, the threat is smaller; you can hold your ground at normal range.
basis: pro:Do not fight an objective one spike behind

when: you have Ignite as a summoner spell
asks: when do I use ignite
should I ignite early or late
do I ignite the support or the adc
when do I press ignite
say: Put Ignite on the target early in the all-in so it cuts their healing the whole fight, or hold it if the kill clearly isn't there.
more: Used at the very end it only finishes a kill. Used at the start it also weakens every heal thrown on that target.
Put it on whoever your marksman is hitting, not on whoever is closest to you.
A wasted Ignite is several minutes where their lane knows your all-in is weaker.
check: Whether they have Heal or a healing support, and whether your marksman is actually following your engage.
breaks: If they have no healing and are likely to escape, save it for the next fight rather than burn it on a target who walks away.

when: the enemy marksman or support has Flash and the player reports it was just used
asks: they burned flash
their adc flashed what now
he has no flash do I go again
they used flash how long do I have
we got the flash
say: Go on that same player again as soon as your engage is back, since they can't dodge it now, or call your jungler in for it.
more: A burned Flash is a lead you have to cash. For the next few minutes that player has no answer to a hook or a dive.
Say it to your jungler: a target without Flash in a duo lane is the best gank on the map.
If nothing happens before it returns, the window is gone and the lane is even again.
check: That the Flash really was used and roughly when, and whether they have another escape ability.
breaks: If the player without Flash now stands behind their minions under tower, do not force a dive for it; take the wave control instead.
basis: pro:Cooldowns spent before the objective decide it

when: the enemy jungler has no recent kill or assist bot side and has not died recently
asks: can I trade if I don't know where their jungler is
is it safe to fight
should I worry about the jungler
do I go in without vision
say: Take short trades and step back afterward while their jungler is unseen, or commit to a long fight only once he shows on the other side.
more: A short trade ends before a jungler can walk in. A long one in the middle of the lane is exactly what a gank needs.
Your own jungler being top does not tell you where theirs is. Only a sighting does.
Once he shows far away, you have a window to play harder, and it lasts about as long as his walk back.
check: When and where their jungler was last seen, and whether your river and tri-bush wards are still up.
breaks: If you have a ward covering the river and it is clear, you can fight longer; the ward is your early warning.
basis: pro:A jungler missing from where he should be is information

when: the enemy jungler is dead
asks: their jungler is dead can we fight
jungler just died bot is free right
do we go in now their jungle is dead
enemy jungle dead what do I do bot
say: Play forward and force the fight or the plates while their jungler is dead, since nobody can gank you, or use the time to ward deep.
more: With their jungler on a respawn timer the lane is a true two against two. If you win that, this is when to prove it.
If the fight is not winnable either, the same seconds buy a safe deep ward that will show his next path to bot.
The window ends when he respawns and walks; do not still be under their tower then.
check: His respawn timer, and whether their mid laner is missing and could come instead.
breaks: If their mid has pushed and disappeared, the lane is not actually free; treat mid as the jungler.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

when: your jungler is alive and the player says a gank is coming bot
asks: my jungler is coming what do I do
jungle is ganking bot how do I set it up
do I engage before he gets here
how do I help the gank
say: Hold your engage until your jungler is in range to follow, or start it yourself first only if they're about to walk out of reach.
more: Engaging early makes it a two against two that your jungler joins late, often after the summoners are already traded.
Before he arrives, let the wave drift toward your side and look harmless. A pushed-up enemy lane is what makes the gank work.
Your crowd control chained after his, not on top of it, keeps the target locked for longer.
check: Where the wave is, whether their lane bush or river is warded, and how far away your jungler really is.
breaks: If they have clearly seen him on a ward and backed off, do not force it under their tower; let him take the push and leave.

when: your team has more kills bot than theirs and your marksman has an item lead
asks: we're winning lane how do I keep it
we're ahead bot what now
how do I snowball this lane
do we dive them
we got kills how do I use it
say: Hold the wave just past the middle and deny them minions, or shove and take plates when their jungler shows on the other side.
more: A lane this far ahead wins by keeping them from farming. They have to walk into you to reach the wave.
Diving is the risky way to extend a lead. A failed dive is the usual way a won lane gets handed back.
Keep river vision up: the stronger you are, the more their jungler and mid want to visit.
check: Where their jungler and mid are, and whether your river ward is alive.
breaks: If they give up the wave entirely and stay under tower, stop waiting and take the plates and a recall instead.
basis: pro:When ahead, let them come to you

when: your health is low and your marksman is healthy
asks: I'm low can I still stay
should I back if I'm half health
I'm low but my adc is fine
do I recall or keep trading
say: Stand behind your marksman out of engage range and keep your abilities for defence, or recall on the next shoved wave if they can dive.
more: A low support in front is the easiest engage in the lane, and your death leaves your marksman alone against two.
Staying back still gives experience and keeps your shield, heal or peel available.
Recalling on a pushed wave costs the least: the minions hit their tower while you are gone.
check: Whether their support has a hook or dash that reaches the back line, and whether the wave can be shoved first.
breaks: If their lane has kill pressure through minions, do not stay at all; your marksman is safer farming alone under tower than defending you.

asks: when do I go in on them
how do I know when to engage
what am I waiting for before I engage
when is it safe to all in
say: Engage right after their support uses the ability that protects their marksman, or hold and just threaten it if that ability is still up.
more: Most supports have one button that stops your all-in: a shield, a knock-back, a hook answer. With it down, their marksman is alone for a few seconds.
Holding your engage is still pressure. A marksman who has to stand far back to avoid you is losing minions.
Count their wave too. A large wave hitting you during the all-in can swing an even fight.
check: Which defensive ability their support just used, and the size of each wave.
breaks: If you cannot tell what was used, wait for a minion they must walk up for and go then instead.

when: you are level 2
asks: how do I all in as Leona
Leona level two what do I do
when do I go in as Leona
Leona combo early
say: Zenith Blade onto whoever steps up, then Shield of Daybreak for the stun, or keep both and zone if their wave is much bigger.
more: Zenith Blade only dashes you to the last champion it hits, so throw it when one of them is in front of the other.
Your Sunlight mark is consumed by your marksman's damage, so the engage is only worth it if they are in range to hit your target.
Once you are in there is no way out. Check the wave and the jungler before the dash, not after.
check: Whether your marksman is close enough to follow, and how many enemy minions will be hitting you.
breaks: If their support can knock you away or shield the target, bait that ability out first or wait for level 3 and Eclipse.

asks: where do I throw hook as Nautilus
Nautilus how do I play lane
do I hook or walk up as Naut
Nautilus engage tips
say: Walk up and root with your first attack when they're close, or throw Dredge Line when a last hit pins them in the open.
more: Staggering Blow roots on your first attack against a target, so simply walking at them is a real threat without spending the hook.
Dredge Line pulls you to terrain too, which makes it your escape. Thrown and missed, you have neither engage nor exit.
At level 6 Depth Charge chases its target, which makes your all-in very hard to dodge. If minions block the hook, keep it.
check: Whether minions stand between you and the target, and whether their jungler could punish you after a missed hook.
breaks: If they stay behind a full wave, stop fishing; hold the hook as a threat and let your marksman farm.

asks: Thresh do I hook or flay
how do I use lantern
Thresh lane what's my job
when do I throw lantern
say: Throw Death Sentence when they're stuck on a last hit, or hold it and keep Flay ready to push away whoever jumps your marksman.
more: Flay knocks enemies in the direction you sweep, so the same button pulls a target toward you or shoves a diver off your marksman.
Dark Passage lets an ally dash to you. Thrown behind you into the river, it brings your jungler into the lane faster than walking.
Souls from enemies dying near you give armor and ability power for good, so staying near the wave has long-term value.
check: Where your jungler is, and whether their support has a dash you should keep Flay for.
breaks: If you already used Flay to engage, you have nothing to stop their counter-engage; go in only when your marksman can win it outright.

asks: Blitzcrank when do I hook
should I just keep throwing grabs
Blitz lane how do I play
I keep missing hooks what do I do
say: Keep Rocket Grab ready and stand where it has a clear line so they give up minions, or throw it when one steps out.
more: An unused grab is the pressure. While it is up, their marksman has to stay behind minions and lose last hits.
A missed grab tells them they can walk forward freely until it returns.
Overdrive gets you into range but slows you afterward, so using it to run in means you cannot easily run back out.
check: Whether minions block the line, and whether pulling this target into you is a fight your marksman wins.
breaks: Do not pull a tank or an engage support into your marksman; if only that target is in range, hold the grab.

asks: Alistar do I engage or peel
how do I go in as Alistar
Alistar combo or save it
what do I do as Ali in lane
say: Headbutt into Pulverize onto their marksman when your own can follow, or keep Headbutt to knock a diver away if you're the weaker lane.
more: Headbutt knocks the target back, so used alone on someone diving your marksman it ends the fight on your terms.
Triumphant Roar charges from stunning or displacing champions and from nearby deaths, then heals you both. Staying near the wave keeps it ticking.
At level 6 Unbreakable Will lets you stand under a tower far longer, which is what makes your dives work.
check: Whether your marksman is in range to follow, and whether you need Headbutt for defence against their engage.
breaks: If you engage and their support peels the target away, you are deep with both abilities down; walk out rather than chase.

asks: Rakan how do I engage
Rakan lane tips
do I go in with W as Rakan
how do I get out after I engage as Rakan
say: Grand Entrance in for the knock-up, then Battle Dance back to your marksman, or stay back and poke with Gleaming Quill if they're waiting for it.
more: Battle Dance flies you to an ally and shields them, so your way out depends on where your marksman is standing. Check before you jump.
Gleaming Quill hitting a champion lets you heal your allies, so landing it keeps the lane healthy without committing.
At level 6 The Quickness charms whoever you touch, which turns the same in-and-out into a real all-in.
check: Whether your marksman is close enough to be your exit, and whether their crowd control is ready for your landing.
breaks: If your marksman is far back or dead, the engage has no exit; poke instead.

asks: Pyke how do I trade
Pyke lane what do I do
how do I not die as Pyke
should I hook or dash in as Pyke
say: Land Bone Skewer, trade, then drop out of sight to heal the damage back, or roam instead if they hold the wave under tower.
more: Gift of the Drowned Ones regenerates damage champions dealt to you while you are hidden, so short trades followed by a bush or Ghostwater Dive favour you.
You cannot gain bonus health, so long fights and tower shots are worse for you than for any other support.
From level 6, Death From Below gives extra gold to an ally who assists, so kills you finish still pay your marksman.
check: Whether a bush or your camouflage is available to heal in, and their crowd control.
breaks: If they have a control ward in the lane bush and point-and-click crowd control, the trade pattern fails; play for roams instead.

asks: Braum how do I trade
Braum what's my job in lane
when do I use the shield as Braum
Braum passive how do I use it
say: Land Winter's Bite or one attack so your marksman can finish the stun, or hold Unbreakable up when their big projectile is coming.
more: Concussive Blows stuns at four stacks, and after your first stack your marksman's attacks add the rest. A fast-attacking partner stuns very quickly.
Unbreakable intercepts projectiles from one direction, so face it toward the ability that would kill your marksman.
Stand Behind Me can jump to a minion as well as an ally, which gets you forward or back out.
check: Whether your marksman is in attack range of the target you marked, and which enemy projectile matters most.
breaks: If their damage is not projectiles, the shield does little; rely on the stun and on standing in front.

asks: Lulu do I shield or poke
Lulu lane how do I play
who do I use polymorph on
Lulu W on my adc or on them
say: Poke with Glitterlance when they step up and keep Whimsy for whoever jumps on your marksman, or put it on your marksman to chase.
more: Help, Pix adds poke when cast on an enemy. Whimsy on an enemy stops them attacking or casting for a moment. Against a diver or an engage support that is the whole fight.
The same button on your marksman gives attack speed and move speed, which is the better use when nobody can reach them.
At level 6 Wild Growth knocks up enemies around the ally you cast it on, so it is both the save and the counter-engage.
check: Whether the enemy has someone who dives, and your mana after poking.
breaks: If you spend Whimsy and the shield on poke, an engage right after has no answer; keep one of them back against all-in lanes.

asks: Janna what do I do in lane
Janna do I trade or just shield
when do I use tornado
how do I play Janna early
say: Shield your marksman as they trade, since Eye of the Storm adds attack damage, or hold Howling Gale for the engage if they can jump you.
more: Eye of the Storm is offence as well as defence: a shielded marksman wins the auto-attack exchange.
Howling Gale interrupts a dash coming at you. Charged in advance from a bush, it is hard to see and dodge.
The shield also works on your tower, which helps hold plates when you are pushed in.
check: Whether their support has an engage worth saving the tornado for, and your mana.
breaks: If you use the tornado to poke, their engage is free for the next several seconds; against all-in lanes keep it.

asks: Soraka how do I lane
Soraka do I just heal
I keep running out of health as Soraka
when do I use Starcall
say: Land Starcall on a champion before you heal, since it gives health back to you, or stay behind and heal less if they can reach you.
more: Astral Infusion costs your own health, so every heal makes you an easier kill. Starcall hits are what pay for it.
Equinox silences enemies inside and roots those still there when it ends. Dropped on your marksman's feet, it stops a dive.
At level 6 Wish heals every ally wherever they are, so watch the other lanes' fights too.
check: Your own health before each heal, and whether they have a hook or dash onto you.
breaks: If you are low and they have engage, stop healing and recall; a dead Soraka heals nobody.

asks: Nami how do I trade
Nami who do I put E on
when do I bubble
Nami lane tips
say: Put Tidecaller's Blessing on your marksman right as they trade, for the extra damage and slow, or keep Aqua Prison to stop whoever dives in.
more: The blessing makes your marksman's attacks and spells slow the target, and a slowed target is far easier to hit with Aqua Prison.
Ebb and Flow bounces between allies and enemies, so cast when both are close to heal and damage with one button.
Your abilities landing on allies give them move speed, which helps both chasing and escaping.
check: Whether your marksman is about to attack a champion, and their engage threat.
breaks: If you throw Aqua Prison first and miss, you have no defence for a while; against engage lanes use it second.

asks: Milio how do I trade
Milio lane what do I do
when do I use campfire
do I kick them as Milio
say: Drop Cozy Campfire on your marksman so they out-range the trade, or hold Ultra Mega Fire Kick to knock back whoever jumps on them.
more: The campfire heals and adds attack range for allies inside, and it follows the ally nearest the cast point. Extra range means free hits.
Your abilities touching an ally make their next damage burn the target, so shield right before they attack a champion.
At level 6 Breath of Life removes crowd control from allies in range, which answers most engage ultimates.
check: Whether their lane has a dive threat to save the kick for, and your mana.
breaks: If their marksman already out-ranges yours by a lot, the campfire will not win the trade; use it to heal through poke instead.

when: you are level 1
asks: Karma level one what do I do
Karma how do I win lane early
do I use mantra right away
Karma poke
say: Use Mantra with Inner Flame for a big early poke on both of them, or keep Mantra for a shield if they can all-in you.
more: Mantra is available from level 1 without a skill point, so you have an empowered ability before anyone else has a second one.
Your damaging abilities shorten Mantra's cooldown, so poke that lands gets you the next one sooner.
The early health lead decides who can contest the push for level 2.
check: Whether they are standing together for the explosion, and whether their support has a level 2 engage.
breaks: If Inner Flame keeps hitting minions, you are only pushing your wave into gank range; hold it for a clear line.

asks: Zyra how do I lane
where do I put seeds
Zyra do I poke or root
Zyra plants tips
say: Plant seeds where they must walk and grow them with Deadly Spines for steady poke, or keep Grasping Roots for whoever engages on you.
more: Seeds turn into plants only when Deadly Spines or Grasping Roots is cast near them, so place the seed first, then the spell.
Plants keep firing after the cast, which wins long trades and makes them walk out of the wave.
Grasping Roots is your only defence. Thrown for poke and missed, you are an easy target for an engage.
check: Your seed count, your mana, and whether their support can reach you.
breaks: If their lane has hard engage, lead with the spines only and keep the root for when they come in.

asks: Brand how do I stun
Brand lane combo
Brand do I just poke
how do I play Brand support early
say: Land Pillar of Flame first, then Sear for the stun while they burn, or just poke with Pillar if they stay behind minions.
more: Sear only stuns a target that is already ablaze, so any other ability has to land before it.
Blaze stacks up to three times on a target, which is why your trades hurt more the longer they stay in them.
Your abilities also push the wave hard. Decide whether you want that before you cast into minions.
check: Whether minions block Sear, and your mana.
breaks: If you are being pushed toward their tower by your own area damage with no ward, aim past the minions or stop casting.

asks: Lux support how do I play
Lux when do I throw binding
do I shield or poke as Lux
Lux lane tips
say: Poke with Lucent Singularity and follow with an attack for the Illumination damage, or keep Light Binding to stop an engage if they have one.
more: Light Binding holds up to two units, so a single minion in front of them does not protect them.
Your damaging spells mark targets and your next attack on them adds bonus damage, so walk up for the auto when it is safe.
Prismatic Barrier shields any ally the wand touches, which helps your marksman through poke trades.
check: How many minions are between you and the target, and whether their support can dive you.
breaks: If their engage support is waiting for your binding to be used, hold it and poke with the singularity only.

asks: Senna how do I lane
Senna do I take souls or trade
how do I trade as Senna
Senna support what's my job
say: Attack every soul that appears near the wave since they're your scaling, or use Piercing Darkness through a minion to hit them and heal your partner.
more: Souls come from units dying near you, so you have to stay close to the wave even when the lane is hard.
Piercing Darkness fires through a target, healing allies and damaging enemies on the line. One cast can do both.
Last Embrace roots the target it latches to and everything nearby after a short delay, which sets up your partner.
check: Whether stepping up for a soul puts you in engage range, and your mana.
breaks: If their lane has a hook, give up souls on the far side of the wave rather than walk through minions for them.

asks: Morgana who do I black shield
when do I use black shield
Morgana lane into engage
do I shield me or my adc
say: Hold Black Shield for their engage and put it on whoever they aim at, or use it freely if their lane has no crowd control.
more: Black Shield absorbs disabling effects until it breaks, so it has to be on the target before the hook or stun lands.
Dark Binding is a long root. Landing it on a support who walked forward is a free trade for your marksman.
Tormented Shadow pushes the wave. Use it when you want push, not by habit.
check: Which enemy ability is the engage, and who it is most likely aimed at.
breaks: If they bait the shield with a small ability first, the real engage follows; do not react to the first thing thrown.

asks: Yuumi do I stay attached
when do I jump off as Yuumi
Yuumi lane how do I play
should I auto as Yuumi
say: Hop off for one attack on a champion when their abilities are down to charge your heal, or stay attached if their hook is ready.
more: Feline Friendship restores health when you hit a champion with an attack or ability, then heals the ally you attach to next.
While attached you cannot be targeted except by turrets, so the only time you can die is while you are off.
Prowling Projectile hits harder and slows more when it travels longer, so curve it rather than fire it point blank.
check: Whether their hook, stun or root was just used, and where your marksman is standing.
breaks: If your marksman is dead or far, you have no safe place to attach; do not hop off at all.

asks: Renata how do I use bailout
Renata lane what do I do
when do I W as Renata
Renata engage or peel
say: Put Bailout on your marksman as the all-in starts so a takedown can save them, or land Handshake first and throw their diver away.
more: Bailout delays an ally's death and can save them if they get a takedown, so it rewards fighting on rather than running.
Handshake roots the first enemy hit and the recast throws them, toward your team to start a fight or away to end one.
Your attacks mark enemies and allies deal bonus damage to marked targets, so auto before your marksman trades.
check: Whether your marksman can actually get a takedown in this fight, and where minions block Handshake.
breaks: If the fight is clearly lost, Bailout only delays it; use Handshake to peel and leave.

asks: Taric how do I stun
Taric lane tips
who do I put W on
Taric how do I engage
say: Keep Bastion on your marksman so Dazzle fires from both of you, or walk up and stun from yourself when they ignore you.
more: Your spells cast from the ally with Bastion too, so the stun has two lines and one of them is at your marksman's range.
Empowered attacks after each spell lower your cooldowns and charge Starlight's Touch, so hitting something between casts matters.
At level 6 Cosmic Radiance makes nearby allies invulnerable after a delay, so it has to be pressed early, before the burst.
check: Where your marksman is standing relative to the target, and your mana.
breaks: If your marksman stands far back, the second stun line is useless; you have to walk up yourself or wait.

asks: Zilean when do I give xp
who do I give experience to
Zilean passive how do I use it
should I level my adc
say: Give your stored experience to your marksman when it finishes their level before a fight, or keep building it for level 6 if lane is quiet.
more: Time In A Bottle lets you finish an ally's level and you receive the same experience, so nothing is lost by giving it.
Hitting level 2 or level 6 before the enemy pair is the strongest use: you get an ability lead they did not see coming.
It also lets a jungler or mid reach 6 early when you roam.
check: Whether you have enough stored to finish their level, and whether a fight is actually about to happen.
breaks: If nobody is close to a level that matters, hold it; a mid-lane level 6 a little later is worth more than a random level now.

asks: Maokai where do I put saplings
Maokai support how do I lane
do I throw saplings in bush
Maokai engage
say: Throw saplings into the lane bushes for strong poke and warning, or keep mana for Twisted Advance when your marksman can follow the root.
more: Sapling Toss is more effective in brush, so the bushes they want to stand in become dangerous for them.
A sapling in the river bush also acts as an early warning for a gank path.
Twisted Advance makes you untargetable during the dash and roots on arrival, so it can dodge an ability on the way in.
check: Your mana, and whether your marksman is in range to use the root.
breaks: If saplings leave you without mana for the root, you have poke but no engage; pick one job for this wave.

when: the enemy support is Leona, Rakan, Alistar, Rell or another champion who engages with a dash
asks: Poppy into engage support
how do I stop their engage as Poppy
Poppy support what do I do
when do I use Poppy W
say: Stand beside your marksman and press Steadfast Presence as they dash in to cancel it, or charge them into a wall if they hesitate.
more: Steadfast Presence stops enemy dashes around you, so an engage that relies on a dash simply fails while it is up.
Heroic Charge stuns only if the target hits a wall, so fight near the lane edges rather than in the open middle.
Picking your buckler back up gives a shield, which wins short trades.
check: Whether their engage is a dash at all, and how close a wall is.
breaks: If their engage is a hook or a ranged stun, the dash block does nothing; play it as a normal tank lane.

when: the enemy support is Blitzcrank, Thresh, Nautilus or Pyke
asks: how do I play against a hook
they have Blitz what do I do
how do I not get hooked
playing against Thresh
hook support matchup
say: Keep minions between you and their hook and trade right after it misses, or give up the far minions if your wave is dying.
more: Their whole lane is that one ability. While it is up, where you stand matters more than anything you cast.
A missed hook is your window: for a few seconds they have no engage, so step up and take a free trade.
As your wave thins there is less cover, so the dangerous moment is when your minions are nearly gone.
check: Where their support is standing, including inside an unwarded bush, and how many of your minions are alive.
breaks: If they hold the lane bush and you have no vision of it, you cannot see the hook coming; ward the bush or stay out of its line.

when: the enemy support is an engage champion and you are an enchanter
asks: how do I lane against Leona
they have engage and I'm an enchanter
enchanter into Nautilus what do I do
how do I not get all inned
say: Stand apart from your marksman so one engage can't catch both, and poke the support as they walk up, or give the wave when you're low.
more: Engage supports win one long fight and lose many short trades. Every auto on them as they approach makes the all-in worse.
Keep your shield or disengage for the moment they commit. Used on poke, it is missing when it counts.
Their strongest moments are level 2, level 3 and level 6. Outside those you can stand a little closer.
check: Their support's level against yours, and whether your disengage ability is ready.
breaks: If they got level 2 or 6 first, do not test it; stand out of range until you match the level.

when: the enemy support is an enchanter and you are an engage champion
asks: how do I beat an enchanter lane
they have Lulu how do I play it
engage into shield support
do I all in the enchanter or the adc
say: Force the all-in early and often before their healing adds up, going on the enchanter if they stand forward, or roam if they out-range you.
more: Enchanters win slow lanes: every trade that ends without a kill gets healed or shielded back.
The enchanter is often the softer target and the one standing forward to poke. Killing them first removes the sustain.
If you cannot reach them at all, your pressure is better spent mid or in river than taking poke.
check: Whether their peel ability was just used, and whether your marksman has the damage to finish.
breaks: If their marksman is far ahead, the enchanter makes them very hard to kill; play for picks with your jungler instead.

when: the enemy support is a poke mage and you are an engage champion
asks: how do I play into Brand support
they have a poke lane and I'm melee
engage into Xerath what do I do
I keep getting poked out
say: Go in at level 2 or right after they spend abilities on the wave, since mages are fragile, or stay out of range until then.
more: Poke lanes win by chipping you before the fight starts. A fight taken at full health against a mage with spells down is yours.
Their own damage pushes the wave toward you, which makes them easy to gank. Tell your jungler.
Standing in the lane bush out of vision means they cannot target you while you wait.
check: Which of their abilities were just used, your health, and whether your jungler is near.
breaks: If you are already below half health, the all-in is gone for now; recall on the next wave and come back full.

when: your marksman is Lucian
asks: how do I play with Lucian
Lucian adc what does he want
supporting Lucian
do I shield Lucian
say: Shield or heal Lucian right as he steps in to trade, since that empowers his next attacks, or land crowd control near him instead.
more: Lightslinger gives his next two attacks bonus damage when an ally heals or shields him, or when a nearby enemy is immobilized.
He trades in short bursts with a dash, so time your button to the moment he goes in rather than after he is hit.
The lane wants an early lead, so the level 2 push matters more than usual.
check: Whether your shield, heal or stun is ready before he dashes in.
breaks: If Lucian is behind, the short-burst pattern stops working; switch to keeping him safe on the wave.

when: your marksman is Caitlyn
asks: how do I play with Caitlyn
Caitlyn adc what's the plan
supporting Cait
do we just poke with Caitlyn
say: Help push with Caitlyn's range for early plates, or land any root or stun so her trap goes under the target for a headshot.
more: A trapped or netted target takes an empowered Headshot, and a trap under someone you have immobilized is close to guaranteed.
Her range lets her hit their marksman for free, so the lane usually pushes. That means river vision is your job.
Tower pressure early pays off a few minutes later when you both can move to mid.
check: Whether your river ward is up while you push, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If you are pushed in without vision and their jungler is unseen, stop at the middle of the lane and let the wave reset.

when: your marksman is Draven
asks: how do I play with Draven
Draven adc what do I do
supporting Draven
do I engage with Draven
say: Look for an early fight while Draven's attacks hit hardest, or protect the spots where his axes land if they out-range him.
more: His kills pay bonus gold based on Adoration, built by catching axes and killing minions. An early kill snowballs him far faster than other marksmen.
He has to walk to where each axe lands, which is predictable. Body-block or threaten whoever tries to punish that.
A Draven who dies with a lot of Adoration loses the chance to cash it, so do not coin-flip when he is stacked.
check: Whether Draven is actually catching axes, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If he is behind and stacking, play for a safe wave and a jungler gank instead of forcing a two against two.

when: your marksman is Kalista and you are level 6 or close
asks: how do I play with Kalista
Kalista ult what do I do
supporting Kalista
she pulled me now what
say: After Fate's Call pulls you, dash into their marksman for the knock-back and follow with your own crowd control, or use it to escape a dive.
more: Fate's Call teleports her bound ally to her and lets them dash to a position, knocking champions back. With an engage support it is a second engage.
Her damage rises when you both hit the same target, so attack what she attacks.
It is also a save: if you are caught, she can pull you out.
check: Whether Kalista bound to you at the start of the game, and whether her ultimate is ready.
breaks: If you are an enchanter, the dash puts you in the middle of them; aim it to knock a diver away instead.

when: the enemy marksman is Samira
asks: how do I play against Samira
they have Samira what do I do
Samira lane matchup
do I engage on Samira
say: Wait for Samira's Blade Whirl before throwing your key projectile, since it destroys missiles, or stay at range because her damage needs melee.
more: Blade Whirl destroys enemy missiles around her, so a hook or skillshot thrown into it is simply gone.
Her attacks deal extra damage in melee range and Wild Rush dashes through an enemy, so she wants you close. Do not give her the body to dash through.
After a champion kill her dash resets, which is how one bad fight becomes two deaths.
check: Whether Blade Whirl was just used, and whether their support can lock you down for her.
breaks: If their support lands crowd control on you first, do not try to fight back near her; walk away from her dash range.

when: the enemy support is Soraka, Sona, Yuumi, Nami or another healer
asks: how do I beat a healing lane
they just heal everything
playing against Soraka
they out sustain us what do I do
say: Stop spending mana on poke they heal back and save everything for one all-in on the healer, or push and roam if no kill is there.
more: Poke only works if it sticks. Against a healer, the mana you spend buys nothing while theirs buys health.
A short, complete all-in beats healing because the heal has a cooldown and the damage comes all at once.
Healers have mana limits early. A lane where they heal constantly is a lane where they are close to empty.
check: Whether you have Ignite, how much mana their healer has left, and your jungler's position.
breaks: If your lane has no burst at all, do not force it; take wave control and vision and wait for your jungler or level 6.

when: before 3:00
asks: when do I ward first
where do I put my first ward
do I ward at the start
when is the first gank coming
should I ward river now
say: Keep your ward until first clears end, close to three minutes, then ward river, or ward the lane bush now if they're hiding in it.
more: A full first clear takes a jungler to about level 4 and ends near river as the crabs spawn at 2:55. That is when the first full-clear gank arrives.
A ward placed at the start of the game has run out or is nearly out by then.
The exception is a short clear: a jungler who skips camps can arrive earlier, mostly on a lane that is pushed up.
check: Which side their jungler started on if anyone saw, and whether your wave is pushing toward their tower.
breaks: If your lane fought hard at levels 1 and 2 and is pushed up, ward earlier; that is exactly the lane a short clear visits.
basis: pro:A lane that fights early without a ward invites a short clear

asks: where do I ward when we're pushing
we're pushed up where does the ward go
where to ward when the wave is at their tower
ward spot when ahead
say: When you're pushed up, ward the river bush or their jungle entrance to see the gank early, or the tri-bush if they've come from behind before.
more: The further forward you stand, the earlier the warning has to be. A ward in the lane bush tells you nothing useful there.
A deeper ward gives more seconds to walk back, but it is riskier to place. Go right after shoving the wave in.
This ward also helps your jungler: it shows whether the river is safe to cross for crab or dragon.
check: Which path their jungler used last time, and whether the wave is shoved in before you walk to place it.
breaks: If their support is missing as you walk up to ward, do not go alone; take your marksman or skip the deep ward.

asks: where do I ward when we're under tower
we're pushed in where do I ward
ward spot when losing lane
they keep diving us where do I ward
say: When you're pushed in, ward the tri-bush behind your tower to see a dive coming, or the lane bush if their support keeps hiding in it.
more: Under your tower the danger comes from behind or from the side, not from the river in front of the enemy.
Seeing a third player early is what lets you clear the wave and stand back before they commit.
River wards are wasted here: you cannot walk out to place them safely and they warn too late.
check: Whether their mid or jungler is missing, and how big the wave coming into your tower is.
breaks: If you see three or more coming and the wave is large, leave the tower rather than defend it; the ward did its job.
basis: pro:A dive runs on minions and one defensive button

asks: do I ward the lane bush or stand in it
who controls the bush
should I sit in the bush
how do I use the lane bush
they're in the bush what do I do
say: Stand in the lane bush yourself when you're the stronger pair, since they can't target what they can't see, or ward it when they hold it.
more: Whoever holds the bush without being seen decides when trades start. For a hook or engage support that is most of the lane.
A control ward in the bush takes it away from them for as long as you can defend it.
If you are the weaker lane, a normal ward there at least shows the engage coming.
check: Whether they have placed a ward in the bush, and whether you can defend a control ward there.
breaks: If they ward the bush every time, you gain nothing by sitting in it; use a sweep or stand on the open side.

when: a dragon is alive or due within a minute
asks: where do I ward for dragon
when do I ward dragon
do I leave lane to ward drake
how do I set up dragon vision
say: Shove the wave with your marksman about a minute before, then ward the pit and river entrance, or stay in lane if you can't push first.
more: Vision placed before the fight is safe to place. Vision placed as the fight starts is how supports die just before objectives.
A support who dies warding hands over the dragon without a fight, so the timing matters more than the exact spot.
Sweeping their ward out of the pit is worth as much as placing yours: it lets your jungler start unseen.
check: Whether your wave is pushed, where their jungler is, and whether your trinket or sweep is ready.
breaks: If their lane has push and yours does not, do not walk into river first; ward from your side and let your jungler decide.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: the enemy jungler is dead or just showed on the top side
asks: their jungler is top can I ward deep
when can I ward their jungle
is it safe to deep ward
should I ward their buff
say: Go place a deep ward on their bot-side camps now while he can't be there, or just push for plates if your wards are already up.
more: A ward on their jungle camps shows where he goes next clear, which is worth more than one more river ward.
Small camps return about 2:15 after they die, so a ward there catches him each time he comes back for them.
It also sets up your own jungler to invade that side later with information.
check: How long ago he was seen or his respawn timer, and where their mid and support are.
breaks: A sighting gets old quickly; if it has been a while or their mid is missing, ward the river instead.
basis: pro:A jungler seen on the far side opens yours

when: your jungler has a level or kill lead over the enemy jungler
asks: how do I help my jungler invade
where do I ward for my jungler
my jungler wants to invade do I go
should I ward their jungle for him
say: Ward their jungle entrance and the nearest camp so your jungler can see before walking in, or follow him in if your wave is pushed.
more: Invades are decided by which lane arrives first. Your ward tells him whether that is yours or theirs.
If you go with him, shove first. A support leaving a wave under tower loses the marksman experience and risks a dive.
The good outcome is a camp and a health lead, then leaving. Staying for a second fight is where invades go wrong.
check: Whether your wave is pushed, and whether their bot lane can leave before you can.
breaks: If their lane has push, do not follow him in; ping him out, because they will arrive first.
basis: pro:An invade ends when the nearest lane arrives

when: you have at least enough gold for a control ward
asks: where do I put a control ward
do I buy control wards
where does the pink go
is a control ward worth it in lane
say: Put it in the tri-bush or river bush on the side their jungler comes from, or in the lane bush if you're fighting over it.
more: A control ward stays until someone kills it, so put it where you can defend it, not as deep as possible.
It also disables their ward there, which is what lets your own jungler gank unseen.
Losing one costs little. Not having one for the whole lane phase costs ganks you never saw.
check: Where your current control ward is, and which bush their jungler has used.
breaks: If they kill it every time for free, move it one bush closer to your tower instead of re-buying into the same spot.

when: your support item has upgraded and now gives you wards
asks: when do I swap to sweeper
should I get oracle lens
do I keep the yellow trinket
when do I change trinket
say: Swap to the sweeping lens on your next recall now that your item holds wards, or keep the ward trinket if your team has no vision.
more: Once the support item gives you wards, the trinket ward is the spare one. A sweep removes their vision, which your item cannot do.
Clearing a ward before a gank or before dragon is what makes those plays work minutes later.
The cost is fewer wards in total for a short while, so place the item wards more carefully.
check: Whether your item has actually upgraded, and whether you are in base to swap.
breaks: If you are far behind and mostly under tower, more wards may help more than sweeping; keep the ward trinket a little longer.

when: your jungler is alive and the player wants a gank
asks: how do I get my jungler to gank
do I sweep before the gank
should I clear wards for my jungler
how do I set up vision for a gank
say: Clear their river or tri-bush ward before your jungler walks through it, or tell him to come through the lane if you can't.
more: Most failed bot ganks were seen on a ward well before they arrived. Removing that ward is your part of the gank.
Do it early. Sweeping at the last second tells them something is coming.
If the ward stays up, a different path can still work, but only if the wave is near your tower.
check: Where they placed their ward if you saw it, and whether your sweep or control ward is available.
breaks: If you cannot find or clear the ward and the wave is pushed to their side, call the gank off rather than waste his time.
basis: pro:Hovering a play that never starts costs the next clear

when: an ally bot laner died in the last minute with the enemy jungler taking the kill or assist
asks: their jungler keeps ganking us
we got ganked again what do I do
where is he coming from
how do I stop the ganks
say: Ward the path he just used and hold the wave nearer your tower for a few minutes, or ask your jungler to wait there for him.
more: A jungler who got a kill bot comes back, usually the same way, usually when his camps are down again.
Small camps return about 2:15 after he clears them, so his visits come in a rhythm you can expect.
Your own jungler hovering for the counter-gank turns his best lane into a trap.
check: Which side he came from, the time of the gank, and where the wave is now.
breaks: If the wave is stuck pushing toward their tower, a ward alone will not save you; thin it slowly and stay back until it turns.
basis: pro:A jungler missing from where he should be is information

when: you have no wards available
asks: I'm out of wards what do I do
no wards left
I can't ward should I back
we have no vision bot
say: Play as if their jungler is near until wards return, keeping the wave on your half, or recall for a control ward on the next shove.
more: Without vision the only safe information is wave position. Near your tower you do not need the ward.
Your marksman's trinket still works. Ask them to place it in river.
A recall for wards on a pushed wave costs little and buys several safe minutes.
check: Whether your marksman still has a ward, and where the wave is.
breaks: If the enemy jungler just showed top, you have a short safe window anyway; use it to shove and recall.

asks: when do I leave lane to ward
is it safe to go ward
can I walk to river to ward
my adc dies when I go ward
say: Leave to ward right after the wave is shoved into their tower, when they must farm, or stay if their support can engage your marksman alone.
more: While their marksman is last hitting under tower, your partner is safe for the seconds you are gone.
Leaving on an even or losing wave makes it one against two, and that is when the engage comes.
Ping that you are going. A marksman who knows will step back for those seconds.
check: Where the wave is, and whether their support is in lane or already missing.
breaks: If their support disappears as you leave, they may be waiting in the river bush; go back to your marksman.

asks: when can I roam mid
is it ok to roam
when is a roam free
should I leave my adc and go mid
when do I roam
say: Roam mid right after your wave crashes into their tower, when your marksman is safest, or stay if they would freeze the next wave on them.
more: A wave under their tower gives the enemy pair something to do and nothing to dive with. That is the cheapest moment to leave.
The roam still costs something: your marksman takes the next wave alone, and you miss that experience.
A roam that gets a kill or a Flash mid often gives your mid laner push, which in turn protects the river next to bot.
check: Where the bot wave is, whether mid's opponent is pushed up, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If your marksman is weak alone or their lane has hard engage, shorten the roam to a ward in river and come back.

when: your marksman is dead or has just recalled
asks: my adc backed should I roam
adc is dead do I go mid
where do I go while my adc is gone
adc recalled what do I do
say: Use the time your marksman is away to walk mid or ward river, or recall with them if you also have gold to spend.
more: You cannot hold the lane alone, so the seconds are free. Mid is close and a second body there can force a Flash.
Recalling together keeps your items even with the enemy pair, which matters more if the lane is close.
Be back when your marksman arrives. A marksman alone in lane on return is how the roam gets punished.
check: How long your marksman will be away, your gold, and whether mid can be reached in time.
breaks: If a large wave is about to hit your tower, stay and collect what you can before it dies to the tower.

when: you have just recalled
asks: do I go back to lane or through mid
should I path mid after backing
roam on the way back to lane
after I recall where do I go
say: Walk through mid on your way back to lane if their mid is pushed up, or go straight bot if your marksman is already there alone.
more: The path from base through mid costs only a few seconds more and arrives from an angle their mid is not watching.
A full-health support with new items showing up mid is a strong gank even without a kill.
The cost is your marksman facing two alone for those seconds.
check: Where the mid wave is, and whether your marksman is already in lane.
breaks: If the bot wave is pushing into your marksman with both enemies there, skip mid and go straight back.

when: between 2:30 and 3:30
asks: do I help with crab
should I go to scuttle
my jungler is at crab do I go
do I leave lane for the river fight
say: Move to the bot river crab as it spawns at 2:55 if your wave is pushing, or stay and send your jungler to the other crab.
more: Both crabs spawn at 2:55 and early river fights go to whichever side's lanes arrive first.
If their bot lane has push, they arrive before you and your jungler is outnumbered. One crab each is a fine result.
Leaving a wave under your tower for a crab costs your marksman minions and experience they will not get back.
check: Which bot wave is pushing, whether their support is already walking, and where your jungler actually is.
breaks: If your jungler is on the top side of the map, there is no bot crab fight for you; stay in lane.
basis: pro:Take the crab on the side where your lanes can move

when: before 4:00 and your jungler is entering the enemy bot-side jungle
asks: my jungler is invading do I help
should I follow the invade
jungler is in their jungle what do I do
do I leave lane to help him invade
say: Follow your jungler in only if your wave is pushed and you'd arrive before their lane, or stay and ping him out if they've got push.
more: An invade is two junglers until a lane shows up. Whoever's support arrives first usually decides it.
If you win the first exchange, leave with it. Waiting for a second fight is when their lane arrives.
Going while your wave is under tower costs minions and leaves your marksman exposed to a dive.
check: Which bot wave is pushing, and whether their support has already left lane.
breaks: If their support leaves first, do not try to race them; warn your jungler and punish their marksman two against one instead.
basis: pro:An invade ends when the nearest lane arrives

asks: I'm a roaming support when do I leave
Bard when do I roam
Pyke roam timing
how often should I roam
say: Leave on each shoved wave and return before the next one meets, or stay for a full wave when your marksman is under pressure.
more: Roaming supports give up some lane strength in exchange for kills elsewhere. The trade only works if bot does not collapse meanwhile.
Short loops are the pattern: river, mid, back. Long trips to the top side cost two or three waves of experience.
A lead made mid or in jungle comes back to bot as dragon control a few minutes later.
check: Your marksman's health and safety, the wave, and whether a target mid or in river is actually reachable.
breaks: If your marksman has died while you were away, stop roaming until the lane is stable again.

asks: Bard do I collect chimes or stay
should I leave for chimes
Bard chimes or lane
when do I pick up chimes
say: Pick up chimes toward river or mid on each shoved wave, since they power your meeps, or skip far ones while your marksman is threatened.
more: Enough chimes make your meeps hit in an area and slow, so they are real power for later fights.
Chimes near mid double as a roam: you arrive on their mid laner from an odd angle with a stun ready.
Leaving a Caretaker's Shrine by your marksman before you go gives them a heal while you are away.
check: Where the chimes are, the bot wave, and whether their support can engage on a lone marksman.
breaks: If your marksman keeps losing health each time you leave, stay for a few waves and take only chimes inside the lane.

asks: should I roam as an enchanter
do enchanters roam
I'm a shield support do I ever leave
Soraka do I roam
say: Stay with your marksman through lane, since your value is on them, or move only with them to dragon when the wave is pushed.
more: An enchanter alone in river is an easy kill and brings no crowd control to a gank.
Your roam is a group move: push, then walk to the objective together with your marksman.
The exception is a short step to ward when the wave is under their tower.
check: Whether your marksman is moving too, and where the wave is.
breaks: If your marksman is dead or in base, a careful ward toward river is fine; a solo trip to mid usually is not.

asks: their mid is low do I go
mid is asking for help
should I gank mid
mid lane is pushed up do I roam there
say: Go mid if their mid laner is pushed past the centre and your bot wave is shoved, or just hover the river so they back off.
more: A kill or a forced recall on their mid gives your team the middle of the map, which makes the next river objective much easier.
Even showing in the river makes a pushed-up mid laner retreat and lose minions.
Approach from behind their wave if you can. Walking down the lane is seen from far away.
check: The mid wave position, their mid's summoner spells, and whether their jungler is nearby.
breaks: If their mid is sitting under tower, there is no play; do not spend a bot wave walking there.
basis: pro:A low or dead enemy mid makes the river yours

when: the enemy support has not been seen in lane and is alive
asks: their support is missing
their support roamed what do I do
do I follow their support
support went mid do I go too
say: Ping it and punish their marksman two against one for plates or a kill, or follow if your mid laner is about to be dived.
more: Following a roam usually arrives second. Taking something bot arrives first and is guaranteed.
Their marksman alone cannot hold the wave against two. Denied minions and plates cost them more than most roams gain.
The danger is that the support is not roaming but waiting in a bush nearby.
check: Whether they showed mid or are simply out of vision, and the state of your wave.
breaks: If nobody has seen them anywhere after a few seconds, assume the lane bush or tri-bush and do not dive.

when: after 8:00, grubs are alive and your jungler is alive
asks: do I go to grubs
should I roam top for grubs
grubs are up do I leave bot
do I help with void grubs
say: Stay bot and hold the dragon side while your team takes grubs, or go only if your marksman has recalled and the wave is shoved.
more: Grubs spawn at 8:00 on the far side of the map from you. The walk costs waves, and grubs only pay off once you reach towers.
While both junglers are top, bot is the lane that gets dived. Keep the wave near your tower.
If their bot lane leaves for grubs, plates and the dragon are your trade.
check: Where their bot lane and jungler are, and whether a dragon is alive.
breaks: If their whole bot lane disappears toward the top side, tell your team and take the tower or dragon instead of chasing.
basis: pro:Price grubs against plates and waves

when: your jungler and mid are both on the top side or a top-side objective was just taken
asks: my team is all top what do I do bot
should I roam top too
we're alone bot now what
everyone's top do we push
say: Hold the wave near your tower and give nothing while your team plays top, or shove once and recall if you both have gold.
more: When your jungler is far away, theirs has only one useful place to go, and it is your lane.
An even trade or a last plate here is not worth being dived three against two.
The lane's job for this minute is to lose nothing. The payoff arrives on the other side of the map.
check: Where their jungler and mid were last seen, and where your wave is.
breaks: If their jungler shows top as well, the pressure is off; you can step up and trade again.
basis: pro:The lane without help gives nothing

when: you are level 6 and their mid laner is level 5 or lower
asks: I have ult should I roam
level six roam mid
do I use my ult mid
Nautilus six do I go mid
say: Take your ultimate mid on the next shoved wave for a near-certain kill, or keep it bot if their lane hits 6 on this wave.
more: A support ultimate arriving in a solo lane is something their mid has no answer for at this stage.
The cost is that bot is without your ultimate until it returns, right when their pair may reach level 6.
A mid kill now usually means your team has first move to the next dragon.
check: The enemy bot laners' levels, the mid wave, and their mid's Flash.
breaks: If their bot lane is level 6 and yours is not, your marksman needs the ultimate more than mid does.

when: you have roamed and your marksman's CS has fallen behind theirs with no kill or assist for you
asks: my roams aren't working
should I stop roaming
I roamed and got nothing
my adc is mad I keep leaving
say: Stop roaming for the next few waves and rebuild the lane with your marksman, or roam only when they have recalled.
more: A roam is a bet. When it pays nothing, the bill is your marksman's minions and experience plus your own level.
Two failed roams usually mean the targets see you coming or the waves were wrong, not that you were unlucky.
A stable bot lane is also what makes the next dragon contestable.
check: The CS and level gap in your lane, and whether mid can actually set up a gank.
breaks: If the last roam burned a Flash, one more visit before it returns is still worth it.
basis: pro:Stop repeating a gank that keeps failing

when: the enemy bot outer tower has fallen
asks: we took bot tower now what
tower is down where do I go
do I stay bot after tower
we got first tower what next
say: Move mid with your marksman to pressure the next tower and the river, or stay one wave to catch the minions before you leave.
more: With their tower gone the bot wave is long and dangerous for two people to push. Mid is shorter and sits next to both objectives.
A duo mid lets your mid laner take the side lane and keeps your marksman safe near help.
Ward their jungle on the way; the fallen tower no longer protects those entrances for them.
check: Where the bot wave is, whether a dragon is due, and where your mid laner wants to go.
breaks: If a dragon spawns within a minute, go to river first and to mid afterwards.

when: before 2:30
asks: do I hit the wave
should I help push as support
do I attack minions level one
am I supposed to hit creeps
say: Hit the first wave with your marksman to win the race to level 2, or leave it alone if you want the wave near your tower.
more: Extra damage on the first minions decides who levels first, and that level is the first real advantage in lane.
The cost of pushing is position: the wave ends up toward their tower as the first clears finish.
Do not take the last hits. Hit minions to low health and let your marksman finish them.
check: What your marksman is doing: if they are only last hitting, they do not want the push.
breaks: If their lane is much stronger early, a pushed wave only walks you into them; let it come to you.

asks: should I be hitting minions
do I push or not
my adc says stop pushing
when should the support help push
say: Help push only when there's a reason, such as a recall, a roam, plates or dragon, or leave the wave alone so it sits safely.
more: A wave you push by habit ends up at their tower, where they farm safely and you are the gank target.
A wave left alone near your side lets your marksman farm safely and makes them walk up to you.
Ability damage counts too: area spells on the wave push it whether you meant to or not.
check: Whether your marksman is trying to hold the wave, and what you would do with a shoved wave.
breaks: If the enemy is about to recall or just died, push hard; that is the reason you were waiting for.

when: you or your marksman hold enough gold for an item component
asks: how do we recall
should we shove before backing
when do we back
do I help push before we recall
say: Shove the wave into their tower together and recall at once so you lose nothing, or back immediately if you're too low to push.
more: Minions that reach their tower die there, and the next wave meets in the middle while you are in base.
Recalling on a wave that is coming toward you gives them a free push and plates.
Buying together keeps both of you on the same item timing as the enemy pair.
check: Your gold and your marksman's, both health bars, and the size of the wave.
breaks: If their jungler is unseen and you are both low, do not stay to push; the wave is cheaper than two deaths.
basis: pro:A lead is not power until it is spent

when: your marksman is dead or in base and a wave is arriving at your tower
asks: do I take the cs when my adc is gone
should I last hit as support
adc is away do I farm
do I let the tower take the wave
say: Last hit what you can under the tower while your marksman is away, or thin the wave gently so it holds just outside tower range.
more: Gold from those minions on you is better than gold on nobody.
If only a few enemy minions arrive, keeping them alive just outside tower range holds the wave there for your marksman's return.
Your support item shares some minion gold with a nearby ally, so save its charges for when they are back.
check: How many minions are coming, and how long until your marksman returns.
breaks: If the wave is large, do not try to hold it; clear it so the tower does not take damage.

asks: when do I use my support item on minions
do I execute the cannon
how do I use the support item charges
which minion do I take with my item
say: Spend a support item charge finishing the cannon minion or one your marksman will miss, or spend them hitting champions if you can't reach the wave.
more: A charge spent finishing a low minion shares gold with a nearby ally, so both of you are paid.
The cannon is worth the most and is the easiest to lose under tower.
Charges come back slowly, so having some ready when the cannon wave arrives matters more than using them the moment they return.
check: Whether your marksman is close enough to share, and which minions are about to be missed.
breaks: If your marksman is not nearby, hold the charge; using it alone wastes the shared half.

asks: they're freezing on us
the wave is stuck at their tower
we can't farm what do I do
how do I break a freeze
say: Walk past the wave together and force them off it if you're the stronger pair, or ask your jungler to come and break it.
more: A wave held just outside their tower makes you walk a long lane to farm, which is where ganks land.
Breaking it means pushing the whole wave into the tower so it resets. Half a push only makes it worse.
If neither is possible, this is a good time for you to roam: the wave is not coming to your tower soon.
check: Where their jungler is, and whether the two of you win a fight next to their minions.
breaks: If you are the weaker pair, do not walk up for it; give those minions, soak experience from range and wait for help.

when: the enemy jungler or mid is missing and a large enemy wave is arriving at your tower
asks: they're going to dive us
big wave coming do we stay
how do I stop a dive
three of them bot what do I do
say: Clear the wave quickly so your tower shoots the divers and keep your crowd control for the first one in, or leave if you're both low.
more: A dive works because the minions take the tower's shots. With the wave dead, the tower turns on whoever attacks you.
Your stun or knock-back on the first diver, under tower, usually kills them. Used early, it is gone when they commit.
Stand apart from your marksman so one ability cannot catch both.
check: How many minions are left, who is missing from the map, and your health.
breaks: If you cannot clear the wave in time and three are coming, give the tower shots and step back; plates are cheaper than two deaths.
basis: pro:A dive runs on minions and one defensive button

when: a dragon is due within about a minute
asks: what do we do with the wave before dragon
do we push before drake
dragon is spawning do I leave lane
wave or dragon
say: Push the bot wave in before the dragon so you reach river first, or stay and catch the wave if you can't shove in time.
more: The pair that pushes first walks to river first, with the other pair stuck under minions or arriving late.
It can cost a little behind you, such as a plate. That is usually cheaper than arriving second to a dragon.
If you cannot get push, say so early. A team that knows can trade for something on the other side.
check: Which wave is bigger, your marksman's wave clear, and whether your jungler is actually coming.
breaks: If their lane already has the push, do not walk into river after them; hold your tower and let the team decide.
basis: pro:The lane that pushes first moves first

when: the enemy jungler has not shown for a while and your CS lead is growing
asks: we're pushed way up is that ok
should we keep pushing
do we back off the wave
we're at their tower is it safe
say: Let the wave come back toward the middle while their jungler is unseen, or keep pushing only with a ward in river and the tri-bush.
more: A lane that is ahead and pushed to the tower is the best gank on the map for their jungler.
Letting the wave drift back costs a few minions and keeps the lead you already have.
With both gank paths warded, the push is fine: you will see him in time to leave.
check: When their jungler was last seen, and whether both of your wards are still alive.
breaks: If he shows on the top side, push hard for plates right away; that is your window.
basis: pro:A jungler missing from where he should be is information

asks: how do I protect my adc's farm
they keep zoning my adc
my adc can't cs what do I do
how do I help my adc farm under tower
say: Stand slightly ahead of your marksman on the side their support is on to block the trade, or step back together if you're being poked out.
more: Your position decides how far forward your marksman can stand. Too far back and they are alone against two.
Under tower, a light hit on a minion can set up a last hit your marksman would otherwise miss.
A marksman who keeps farming through a hard lane is still on time for their first item.
check: Where their support is standing, and your own health.
breaks: If standing forward just gets you poked low for free, the lane cannot be held there; let the wave come to your tower.

when: the enemy bot laners have both just died or recalled
asks: they both backed what do we do
nobody's in lane do we push
free lane what now
they're both dead do we take tower
say: Push the wave into their tower and hit plates while nobody defends, or shove and recall if their jungler could arrive before the tower drops.
more: An empty lane is the one time pushing has no downside in lane itself: every minion lost to the tower is theirs.
Staying too long turns it around. They return with items while you are low on health and mana.
A ward toward their jungle while you are there keeps the next minutes safe.
check: Their respawn timers or how long since they left, and where their jungler is.
breaks: If you are both low and their jungler is unseen, take one wave and leave rather than staying for a second.
